chunks: I heard Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) saying:
'Zuhd (asceticism) in the world is [comprised of] shortening of hope, gratitude for every blessing, and restraint (wara') from everything that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden.'

key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: zuhd — worldly detachment or asceticism, one of the central virtues in Islamic spirituality
key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: wara' — scrupulous restraint from that which is forbidden or doubtful; a higher degree of caution beyond mere avoidance of the haram
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for Allah combining 'azza (He is Mighty) and jalla (He is Majestic)
key_terms.قَصْرُ الْأَمَلِ: shortening of hope — limiting one's worldly ambitions and not being deceived by long-term worldly expectations

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of zuhd (asceticism) according to Imam Ali in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Abu al-Tufayl, a companion of both the Prophet and Imam Ali (AS), reports this defining statement on zuhd (worldly detachment) from the Commander of the Faithful. Imam Ali (AS) defines zuhd not as withdrawal from the world but as a balanced spiritual orientation comprising three integrated practices: limiting one's worldly ambitions (qasrul-amal), expressing active gratitude for God's gifts, and maintaining scrupulous avoidance of the prohibited. This tripartite definition is addressed to the Muslim community to clarify that true asceticism is not monasticism but a positive ethical stance grounded in submission to Allah.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Maalik Bin Atiyya, from Marouf Bin Kharbouz, from Abu Al Tufayl who said, 
‘I heard Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘الزُّهْدُ’ the ascetism in the world is the reduction of hopes, and appreciating every Bounty, and the restrain from everything what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Prophibited’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah from M’aruf ibn Kharbudh from abu al-Tufayl who has said the following: “I heard ‘Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Zuhd (restraint from worldly matters) in the world is to shorten one’s hopes, give thanks for every bounty and restrain from everything that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made unlawful.’”
